claim.text: Is the statement described in this narrative hearsay under FRE 801(c)?

arguments.text: The drawing was made on the stand during testimony, meaning it is an in-court statement rather than an out-of-court statement. Under FRE 801(c), hearsay requires an out-of-court statement, so this fact directly attacks the claim that the drawing is hearsay.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) defines hearsay as a statement that the declarant makes when the declarant is making the statement; or adopts; or perceives and makes a mental manifestation of; and is offered in evidence to prove the truth of the matter asserted. Crucially, it must be made out of court.
arguments.evidence_span: the drawing the witness made on the stand during testimony

arguments.text: The drawing is offered to prove the faultiness of the designed house. This addresses whether the statement is offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted, which is a necessary element for hearsay, but is secondary to the in-court timing.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) requires that the statement be offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted.
arguments.evidence_span: On the issue of the faultiness of the designed house

arguments.text: The drawing is a visual representation made by a witness during testimony. In-court demonstrations and drawings are generally not considered hearsay because they are subject to contemporaneous judicial observation and cross-examination.
arguments.legal_rule: Evidentiary principle that in-court statements or demonstrations are not hearsay because they occur under oath and are subject to cross-examination.
arguments.evidence_span: the drawing the witness made on the stand during testimony
